observation.visible_scene: Five identical mechanical metronomes (maroon bodies, white dial faces, thin pendulum rods with sliding weights) stand upright in a row on a long white foam plank. The plank rests on two metal cans lying on their sides, which act as rollers, on a light wooden tabletop against a flat teal wall. Bright specular highlights on the can ends are reflections, not separate objects. The camera viewpoint is fixed; the wall, table edge and can positions stay in place throughout.
visible_changes: The pendulum rods of all five metronomes swing continuously side to side (motion blur on the rods and weights), an already ongoing oscillation at both the first and last frame.

The relative phases of the five metronomes change over the excerpt: in early frames (e.g., 1-5) the rods point in mixed directions (some left, some right, some near vertical), while in later frames (e.g., 31-32, 35-36, 39, 41) the rods of the right-hand metronomes swing together in the same direction and cross vertical at nearly the same time, i.e. the swinging becomes progressively more aligned/in unison.

The white plank and the two cans remain essentially stationary in position and orientation; no clear horizontal translation or tilt of the platform is discernible frame-to-frame, so the dominant visible motion is the pendulum swinging and its phase alignment rather than platform movement.
The metronome bodies keep a constant spacing and the same relative positions on the plank throughout; no object enters or leaves the scene.
outside_clip_unknowns: The initial conditions before t=0 (whether the metronomes were deliberately started out of phase) are not shown.
The final steady state after the last frame (full synchronization or continued drift) is not shown.
Any unseen coupling mechanism or operator that produces the phase alignment is not visible.
uncertain_details: Whether the platform rocks or shifts by a small amount is not confidently visible; the apparent positions of plank and cans are nearly constant.
The synchronization is partial/progressive within the excerpt rather than a single clean locked state; exact phase differences between metronomes are hard to read from the blur.
Minor differences in pendulum weight settings between units are not reliably distinguishable.
